ops.text:
One session's landings across nine repos, recorded so the next agent does not rediscover any of it. The governing constraints were the user's: make it correct for a first install, delete cruft rather than chase upgrades, assume nobody but this fleet has anything installed, and verify capt-hook after every change.

## Released

| repo | version | what it carries |
|---|---|---|
| fusekit | v1.20.0 | `(*LocalTenantController).DesiredSourceFleet` — reads an owner's published fleet back without publishing |
| synckit | v0.39.0 | drops the pre-v0.21 legacy LaunchAgent sweep; cut ahead of daemonkit's `RemoveUnmarked` deletion |
| captain-hook | v12.22.5 | the whole install-path fix (below) |
| cc-runtime | v0.18.0 | migrated onto the daemonkit v0.23 surface; synckit repinned to v0.39.0 |
| cc-pool | v0.69.0 | the source-fleet wedge fix and `ccp package reset` |

Landed unreleased: cc-patch (dead `.meta.json` sidecar), daemonkit (fleet gate, `RemoveUnmarked` retirement, a `replace (`-block parser fix).

## The three things that actually mattered

**1. captain-hook's install path lied, and `brew upgrade` failed on every host.** The formula's `post_install` shelled `capt-hookd package-install`, whose last step writes `~/Library/LaunchAgents/<label>.plist` — denied by Homebrew's post-install sandbox. It failed *after* the app bundle was superseded, so the deployment converged anyway and only the exit code was wrong, which is why it survived for weeks. Deleting `post_install` alone would have broken the self-updater and fresh install, since it was the only thing deploying the app; the deploy moved into a shared `deploy()` that both `capt-hook helper install` and `run_update` call, outside any sandbox. Verified live: `brew upgrade` exits **0** (was 1), `helper install` superseded cleanly and reported the version *the host answered with*, all four copies converged to 12.22.5, and the runbook's full four-event heartbeat ledger came back.

**2. cc-pool crash-looped 23,269 times on `catalog: tenant generation mismatch`.** Every runtime start republished the compiled topology at a hardcoded generation 1, which fusekit's catalog refuses unless the generation strictly advances. Fixed with a read-then-compare gate plus one re-read behind a race winner. Both halves carry independent mutation brackets that reproduce the incident's own error when removed.

**3. The release gate silently omitted two live consumers.** `cc-runtime` and `cc-squash` pinned daemonkit v0.19.1 and were in none of the three places the fleet set lived. Both are now in `ci/fleet-refs.txt`, the workflow matrix is *generated* from that file (the hardcoded copy is deleted), and a real GitHub run confirmed `fleet-set` expands all 16 legs.

## Deliberately not built, with the reason

- **`cc-interact daemon.Launcher.Paths` deletion — cancelled.** Premise refuted three ways: four repos set it (not one), the second cited line was a different live field whose deletion would have broken cc-present's channel setup, and the validate clause is a fail-fast guard cc-review and cc-present assert on purpose.
- **Routing `ErrUntrusted` to `settle` — investigated, not landed.** One line, bracketed green→red→green, then two CONFIRMED security defects: it conflates a server-side authz denial with a client-side trust refusal, and widens a same-UID forged-record bypass past `requireEmpty`.
- **The cc-pool generation advance — written, then reverted.** `resolveClaudePhysicalPolicy` hard-pins `FleetGeneration` to a compile-time 1, so advancing to generation 2 would have wedged the daemon permanently; the lane's own tests asserted that end state.
- **`ccp package reset` clearing the fusekit catalog — documented instead.** A destructive verb reaching into another product's store is not a change to make on a reviewer's suggestion.

## Open, with full traces filed

`3795f7c2` (the `FleetGeneration` pin — a real topology change still cannot converge), `2ccd7f68` (deploy cannot stop an untrusted daemon), `b9c8fecf` (cc-squash's remaining test port; its production code is migrated and the fleet leg passes), `a7a5ac49` (release ordering for daemonkit's `RemoveUnmarked` deletion), `3197b2a3` (an `internal/wire` phase-bleed flake), `6b477957` (fleet-build.sh has no test coverage), `e240c0b5` (forge-studio's expired OAuth blocks the runbook's proof step there).

## Backlog reconciliation

43 open tasks were re-verified against `origin/main`. Only 2 were closable; **34 are genuinely still open**, 7 need an owner decision. The premise that the backlog was mostly stale was wrong — it is mostly real work.
